answer: To resist sybil attacks, each agent must lock a unique non-fungible anchor inside its private vault, which is then tied to an orchard of previously graded original answers that peers have attested. An attacker creating N fake identities must independently grow and maintain N separate orchards of validated work, because the anchors cannot be shared or bulk-produced; the cost in real judgment time therefore scales linearly with the number of sybils and cannot be parallelized cheaply across a farm.
